data.sentence: Thanks for calling Aegis Cloud Security support, this is Marcus Williams.
Hi Marcus, Mina Joshi from Axiom Labs, and Ryan Caldwell is on too. We're calling about our June invoice.
It's the first one on the new three-year contract, and it's about eleven thousand eight hundred dollars higher than we expected.
I'm sorry about that. Let me pull it up — do you have the invoice number?
Got it. Can you walk me through what you expected versus what you see?
The whole point of the elastic seat model was that we pay for our monthly average seats, not our peak.
We had a hackathon in May and spun up about two hundred temporary accounts for three days, and we've been billed as if they existed all month.
I see it. The invoice is calculated on peak seats — two thousand and eighty — instead of the monthly average, which comes to about one thousand eight hundred and ninety.
And there's a second problem. The enterprise API tier appears twice, once as a line item and once inside the platform bundle.
Yes, I see the duplicate. That one's clearly an error.
Honestly, Marcus, this is disappointing. We signed in April because the elastic model fit how we work, and the very first invoice ignores it.
I had to explain this to our CFO this morning, and she asked whether we read the contract correctly. We did.
You did. Your contract clearly states monthly average for elastic seats. This is on our side.
Let me check one thing. It looks like your account was moved to the new contract, but the billing profile still has the old seat calculation.
We've seen something similar with accounts migrated during the Comply v2 launch, so I suspect it's the same migration problem.
So are other elastic customers getting wrong invoices too?
That's a good question, and I'm going to ask billing operations to check every elastic-seat account before the next cycle.
What happens with this invoice? Our payment run is on the twentieth.
I'll void INV-2026-03412 and issue a corrected invoice based on the average seat count, with the duplicate API line removed.
You'll have it within five business days, well before your payment run. Don't pay the current one.
Okay, that works. Can I get that in writing for our CFO?
I'll email a confirmation today with the corrected amount, the reason for the error, and the case number.
And going forward, can we see seat counts ourselves before the invoice lands? We'd have caught this.
Not in the console today, but there's a usage page in the works. I'll pass your request on to product.
Please. To be clear, we're happy with the platform itself. It's the billing side that keeps letting us down.
Understood. I'll also let Aisha know, so she can follow up from the account side.
Thanks, Marcus. I appreciate you owning it quickly.
